subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In simple harmonic motion, the acceleration is:
options: Proportional to displacement and directed towards equilibrium
questions.explain: SHM is defined by a = -(omega^2)x: acceleration is proportional to, and opposite in direction to, displacement.

questions.q: The restoring force in SHM is always directed:
questions.explain: A restoring force towards equilibrium is what produces oscillation.

questions.q: The time for one complete oscillation is the:
questions.explain: Period T is the time for one full cycle; frequency f = 1/T.

questions.q: A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 40 s. Its period is:
questions.explain: T = total time / number of oscillations = 40/20 = 2.0 s.

questions.q: If the period of an oscillation is 0.25 s, its frequency is:
The maximum displacement from equilibrium in SHM is the:
questions.explain: Amplitude is the peak displacement from the equilibrium position.

questions.q: For a mass on a spring, the period is given by:
questions.explain: Increasing mass increases period; a stiffer spring (larger k) decreases it.

questions.q: For a simple pendulum, the period depends on:
options: The length and gravitational field strength
questions.explain: T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g); for small angles it is independent of mass and amplitude.

questions.q: If the length of a simple pendulum is quadrupled, its period:
questions.explain: T is proportional to sqrt(L), so quadrupling L multiplies T by 2.

questions.q: In SHM, the velocity of the oscillator is maximum at:
questions.explain: Speed is greatest at equilibrium and zero at the extremes of the motion.

questions.q: In SHM, the acceleration is maximum at:
questions.explain: Acceleration is greatest where displacement (and restoring force) is greatest, i.e. at the amplitude.

questions.q: During SHM, energy is continually exchanged between:
questions.explain: Total mechanical energy stays constant (ignoring damping); KE is maximum at equilibrium, PE at the extremes.

questions.q: At the amplitude position of an undamped oscillation, the energy is:
questions.explain: At maximum displacement the oscillator is momentarily at rest, so all energy is potential.

questions.q: The total energy of an undamped SHM oscillator is proportional to:
questions.explain: Energy is proportional to amplitude squared, so doubling amplitude quadruples the energy.

questions.q: Damping of an oscillation causes the amplitude to:
options: Decrease over time as energy is dissipated
questions.explain: Damping forces (e.g. friction, air resistance) remove energy, reducing amplitude.

questions.q: A mass-spring system has its mass quadrupled. Its period:
questions.explain: T is proportional to sqrt(m), so quadrupling m multiplies T by 2.

questions.q: Angular frequency omega is related to period T by:
questions.explain: Angular frequency = 2*pi times the frequency = 2*pi/T.

questions.q: At the equilibrium position of SHM, the displacement and acceleration are:
questions.explain: At equilibrium x = 0, so a = -(omega^2)x is also zero, while velocity is maximum.

questions.q: A defining condition for SHM is that the frequency is:
questions.explain: For SHM the period and frequency do not depend on the amplitude.

questions.q: A pendulum on the Moon (weaker g) compared with Earth would have a period that is:
questions.explain: T = 2*pi*sqrt(L/g); a smaller g gives a longer period.
